title: Software Engineer, New Grad
description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works. Your role Stripe is large enough that individual products and projects can be rapidly deployed to a meaningful fraction of the world’s businesses, but small enough that individual agency still has outsized impact. Small teams can impact how millions of businesses grow. Right now the global economy is replatforming around AI, creating new opportunities for growth. We’re at the center of this, and we think the best work is still in front of us. title: Head (Senior Manager) - Industrial Relations
description:
About the Team
You will join the Security & Investigations team within Fulfilment & Experience (F&E) at Meesho. F&E is the operational and technological backbone powering India's cost-efficient, reliable and scalable e-commerce network, serving 100M+ monthly active users. From enabling Valmo's distributed logistics network to building scalable fulfilment and experience platforms, F&E operates at the intersection of technology, operations and network innovation.
Within F&E, the Security & Investigations team safeguards the integrity and resilience of this network. The team investigates shipment loss, pilferage, fraud and misconduct, oversees physical security across operating sites, and coordinates with law enforcement and other stakeholders where required. Working closely with Operations, HR, Legal and logistics partners, the team helps keep the network secure, compliant and resilient.
About the Role
Valmo's operating network is powered by a large and diverse workforce spanning sort centres, hubs and last-mile operations. A significant portion of this workforce is engaged through logistics partners and other workforce arrangements, creating a complex industrial-relations environment across multiple locations and states.
As Head – Industrial Relations, you will own the Industrial Relations (IR) charter for the operating network, within the Security & Investigations function, and work closely with HR, Legal, Operations and partner leadership. Your mandate will be to build a stable, compliant and scalable workforce-relations framework that prevents avoidable disputes, enables fair and timely resolution of workforce issues, and provides strong governance when matters escalate.
The role combines strategic IR leadership with significant field engagement. You will build early-warning mechanisms, manage worker and union relationships, oversee dispute and disciplinary processes, strengthen partner workforce compliance, engage with labour authorities, and create playbooks and governance mechanisms that can scale with the network. What You Will Do Own IR strategy and governance. Build and continuously evolve a national IR framework covering workforce relations, grievance management, dispute prevention, statutory compliance, worker/union engagement, escalation and resolution. Build workforce intelligence and early-warning mechanisms. Track workforce sentiment, grievances, absenteeism, wage-related concerns, shift and working-condition issues, emerging worker representation or union activity, and other indicators of potential disruption across the network. Prevent and manage industrial disputes. Develop structured approaches to prevent disputes and lead the response to strikes, work stoppages, protests, gheraos and other workforce disruptions. Engage with worker representatives and union leaders and coordinate with Operations, HR, Legal, partners, local administration, labour authorities and law enforcement, as appropriate. Bring IR rigour to investigations. Partner with Security & Investigations, HR and Legal on cases involving employees or partner workers, including theft, fraud, misconduct and policy violations. Ensure due process, appropriate documentation and legally sound decision-making. Govern disciplinary processes. Oversee show-cause notices, domestic enquiries and disciplinary actions, ensuring that processes are fair, consistent, timely and legally defensible under applicable law, standing orders and organisational policy. Drive partner workforce compliance. Establish and monitor governance over logistics partners covering contract labour requirements, wage and benefits compliance, statutory registrations, working hours, worker documentation, grievance mechanisms and other applicable labour requirements. Drive timely corrective action and escalation where gaps are identified. Own government and authority engagement. Build effective working relationships with labour departments, labour commissioners, conciliation officers and other relevant government authorities. Represent the organisation in inspections, conciliation proceedings and hearings, in partnership with Legal, and coordinate with Security on matters requiring law-enforcement engagement. Build effective grievance and escalation channels. Design and strengthen mechanisms such as worker helplines, site-level committees, grievance forums and escalation paths so that workforce concerns are surfaced and resolved before they become formal disputes. Create scalable IR playbooks and capability. Develop SOPs, policies, escalation matrices and response playbooks for dispute management, investigation-linked disciplinary action, partner workforce issues and authority engagement. Train site leaders, partner supervisors, HR teams and security personnel on relevant IR practices and labour-law basics. Build IR analytics and leadership reporting. Establish dashboards and regular reviews covering incidents, disputes, grievances, compliance health, partner risks, resolution timelines, repeat issues and emerging trends. Translate these into clear insights and actions for senior leadership. Strengthen cross-functional governance. Establish clear interfaces between IR, HR, Legal, Operations, Security & Investigations and partner leadership, including decision rights, escalation threshold What You Will Need 8–15 years of experience in industrial relations, employee relations, labour relations or labour-law compliance, preferably in large, distributed workforce environments. Experience in logistics, e-commerce, manufacturing, warehousing, retail, infrastructure or other large blue-collar and/or contract-workforce environments is strongly preferred. Deep working knowledge of applicable Indian labour and employment laws, including the Labour Codes and associated rules/notifications, contract labour requirements, industrial disputes, standing orders and relevant state-specific requirements. Practical experience applying labour law and IR principles on the ground across multiple sites and, ideally, multiple states. Proven experience handling industrial disputes, worker grievances, union/worker representative engagement, negotiations, strikes or work stoppages. Experience conducting or overseeing domestic enquiries and disciplinary proceedings, with a strong understanding of how employee investigations intersect with employment law and due process. Experience managing contract labour or partner workforce compliance, including audits, statutory requirements, wage-related compliance and remediation. Strong ability to engage with labour authorities, conciliation officers and other government stakeholders, preferably with experience representing an organisation in formal proceedings. Strong negotiation, conflict-resolution and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to remain calm, credible and objective in high-pressure situations. Ability to work effectively across HR, Legal, Operations, Security & Investigations and external partners, with sound judgement on ownership, escalation and confidentiality. Strong communication skills in English and Hindi. Proficiency in one or more regional languages is an advantage, particularly for workforce-heavy operating regions. Strong analytical and problem-solving ability, including the ability to use workforce and incident data to identify patterns, risks and preventive actions. Willingness to travel extensively across operating locations and respond to sensitive on-ground situations at short notice. High integrity, discretion and maturity, with the ability to handle confidential matters and decisions that can materially affect employees and workers. A degree in law, HR, labour welfare, social work or a related discipline (LLB, MSW, MBA-HR or equivalent) is preferred. Role Characteristics National scope with significant field engagement across the operating network. High level of cross-functional and external stakeholder interaction. Combination of strategic programme ownership, operational problem-solving and on-ground dispute management. Requires sound judgement, neutrality, confidentiality and the ability to balance business continuity with fair and compliant workforce practices.

title: ML Engineer (Training Infra), Foundational Models
description:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.



About the Role

You will own the infrastructure that our next family of foundational models is trained on. This is a deep systems role: distributed training at scale, parallelism strategies, GPU kernel work, throughput and stability optimization, and the unglamorous reliability engineering that determines whether a frontier training run actually finishes.

The bar is high. A bad MFU number, a slow data loader, a switch flap — these are problems whose cost is measured in weeks and millions of dollars. You will be expected to find them before they happen, and to fix them fast when they do.

What You’ll Do

 - Build, maintain, and continually push the limits of our distributed training stack across large GPU clusters.

 - Design and implement parallelism strategies — data, tensor, pipeline, sequence, expert — and reason about which combinations make sense for which architectures and which scales.

 - Profile and optimize end-to-end training throughput: kernel performance, communication overlap, memory layout, checkpointing, data loading.

 - Write and tune custom GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton) where off-the-shelf is leaving performance on the table.

 - Own the reliability of long-running training jobs — fault tolerance, checkpoint integrity, deterministic restarts, automated detection of slow nodes and silent corruption.

 - Partner closely with researchers to make sure architectural ideas can actually be trained efficiently, and with the data team to keep the pipeline from being the bottleneck.



What We’re Looking For

 - BS or MS in Computer Science or a closely related technical field (or equivalent demonstrated experience).

 - 3+ years of experience building ML training infrastructure or large-scale distributed systems. Exceptional early-career candidates with a strong systems background will be considered.

 - Hands-on experience training large models with distributed training frameworks — Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, FSDP, NeMo, or equivalent. You should have been on-call for a real pretraining run.

 - Deep working knowledge of GPU architecture, the CUDA programming model, and standard tools for profiling GPU workloads (Nsight, PyTorch profiler, etc.).

 - Strong PyTorch internals knowledge. You're comfortable reading and modifying low-level training code, not just using high-level APIs.

 - Meaningful open-source contributions in the training infrastructure ecosystem — Megatron, DeepSpeed, PyTorch, vLLM, Triton, NCCL, or similar.

Bonus Points

 - Custom CUDA or Triton kernel development with measurable wins on real workloads.

 - Direct experience training models at 10B+ parameters or on 1000+ GPU clusters.

 - Familiarity with cluster orchestration and job scheduling (Slurm, Kubernetes) at scale.

 - Experience with mixed precision (BF16, FP8), quantization-aware training, or other numerical work that has shown up in production training runs.

 - First-author papers or technical reports on training systems, scaling, or model efficiency.

Why this role?

Frontier model training is one of the hardest systems problems in the world right now, and most of the people doing it well sit at a small handful of labs. You will be doing the same work, with the same autonomy, and your impact will be visible in every model Sarvam ships.

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

 - Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

 - High ownership and high impact, from day one

description:

We are hiring a Software Engineer to own major parts of this platform end to end, working closely with the Staff Engineer who leads its architecture. You will take an area such as speech to text pipeline,or text to speech pipeline, and be accountable for its reliability, performance and end-to-end latencies. This role is for someone who is obsessed with latencies, optimizes services and network paths to shave off milliseconds, ships fast, reasons from first principles, and treats AI as the default way to get engineering work done.


What you will do


Own a platform area end to end

• Own one or more major parts of the platform, such as the WebSocket streaming layer, a speech recognition pipeline, or text to speech pipeline: build, operate and improve them.

• Turn loosely defined goals into RFCs, milestones and shipped results, and write down the decisions and trade-offs.

• Be accountable after launch: on-call, incident response, root-cause analysis and follow-through on fixes.

• Make the call when a decision is needed, and own the outcome.

• Obsessed with latencies, dissecting existing services to understand the system, and tuning the right knobs to optimize performance.

• Bring services across without regressions in customer-facing APIs, latency or reliability.


Build real-time and model-serving pipelines

• Build and operate streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, long-lived sessions queue-based batch processing, backpressure and low-latency model invocation.

• Engineer audio pipelines: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate conversion and format encoding, and VAD-based silence detection for ASR.

• Hold your services to sub-100ms latency SLOs in a multi-tenant environment, and know where every millisecond goes.


Think in systems and from first principles

• Reasons from constraints: latency budgets per hop, throughput, cost per request, failure modes and tenant isolation.

• Use back-of-the-envelope estimates to decide what to build, what to optimize and what to leave alone.

• Prefer simple designs you can fully explain over clever ones you cannot.

• Build in observability from day one: logging, metrics and tracing that let anyone debug production quickly.


Raise the bar for the team

• Strengthen the integration testing harness so the team can ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs.

• At least one service you owned end to end under real load, including what broke and what you changed.

• Strong distributed-systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, queues, caching, consistency and failure modes.

title: Software Development Engineer - Tejas
description:
Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends.

Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. The memory side lets agents remember what they learn over time, about individual users, about teams, and across the organisation. We want both to keep improving as they are used.

Knowledge and memory for agents is a rapidly evolving field. We want to build at the frontier of it, and to show with measurable results that our approach does better than traditional ones.



ABOUT SARVAM

Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.



WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU

You will join a small team and own large parts of the platform. The work is driven by real customer deployments, so what you build gets used quickly and you see what works and what does not. You will also work closely with the teams building Sarvam's models, document AI and inference, which makes it much easier to solve problems that cut across the stack.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and run the ingestion pipeline that parses, extracts and indexes large volumes of documents, and keep it reliable when files are messy and external services fail.

 - Connect to databases and enterprise systems so agents can work with structured records as well as documents.

 - Design how enterprise data is modelled, including the ontology, matching the same entity across sources, and tracing every value back to where it came from.

 - Build the retrieval tools agents call, with search, filters and citations, and make them fast and cheap enough for agents to use heavily.

 - Build memory for agents at the level of a user, a team and the whole organisation: how it is written, stored, retrieved and kept accurate over time.

 - Run evals, find where answers go wrong, and keep iterating until quality improves.

 - Work with product and forward-deployed engineers to turn what one customer needs into something the platform does for every customer.

 - Write design docs and keep decisions documented.

Our production stack is Go, with Temporal, OpenSearch and Postgres.



WHO YOU ARE

We are hiring at 3 to 5 years of experience.

 - You have built and run backend or data systems in production, and you have fixed them when they broke.

 - You are strong in at least one backend language. Our core is in Go, so Go experience is a plus, and you should be happy to work in it every day.

 - You have good fundamentals in data modelling and PostgreSQL.

 - You have worked on long-running pipelines and know how to make them safe to retry and recover.

 - You have worked on search or retrieval and know how to debug why the right result did not come back.

 - You use AI coding tools every day and have a good sense of where they help and where they don't.

 - You care about measuring quality, and you are comfortable building the evals to do it.


BONUS POINTS

title: APM - integrations
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Composio builds the AI-native automation layer for software teams: SDKs, runtimes, and platform tooling that let developers compose, evaluate, and operate agentic workflows and AI-powered products. Our systems must be reliable at scale - agents must act correctly, integrations must be robust, and integration needs to be an autonomous, observable function that accelerates engineering rather than slowing it. You'll join a small, high-leverage team building the delivery systems and metrics that give product and support teams visibility and predictable delivery.

This role is based in Bangalore (HSR).



WHO IS OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE?

A high-agency operator who is also AI-native, and who wants to grow into product. The role starts ops-heavy: you run the operations that get apps live on Composio, keep the toolkits healthy, and automate as much of that work as you can. Over 6-8 months, once those workflows and automations are running, the role shifts towards owning ambiguous product problems across the platform - triggers, tools, skills, auth, governance, and toolkit-level issues like rate limits and MCP hosting. This is not a traditional PM role with an engineering team to direct. It's closer to founder-mode ownership of a product line, where you solve problems using agents and a small ops team.

You've shipped things on your own - a side project, a tool, a micro-business, or a system you built that is still running - and you've run real operations with quality bars, not just executed inside someone else's process. You're at the edge of AI out of genuine curiosity: you use AI tools daily and can point to specific things you built or automated with them in the last month. You pick work by impact, not by how interesting it is, and you have no ego about manual work that isn't automated yet. You can hold a technical conversation with engineers without a translator, and you're comfortable owning problems that don't have a clear owner yet.



WHAT WILL THEY OWN?

 - The toolkit number: how many apps are live on Composio, and the health of the ones already live.

 - New apps, end to end: run the operations of getting them live - research, setup, QA, launch.

 - Existing toolkits: make them better with the product team, and clear the issues that stop them from working well.

 - QA and support for every toolkit you bring live. Once it's live, its quality is your problem.

 - The ops playbook: build it, run it, scale it. SOPs, small tools, AI agents before humans - you automate yourself first, and when scaling takes people, hiring them is part of the job.

 - The metrics for this function: define them, build them, watch them.

 - Product problems, as the ops layer starts running on its own: ambiguous, non-engineering problems across triggers, tools, auth, governance and toolkit-level issues - scoped, owned and shipped by you.



WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

 - Experience: 2-4 years. We care more about how fast you've grown than how senior you are.

 - Technical floor: can explain what an API and an integration are, reads API docs cold, writes enough code to build small tools and automations. Not an engineer; infra-level work is not the job.

 - AI-native automation instinct: your default answer to repeated work is "how do I never do this manually again" - backed by recent, specific evidence of things you've built or automated with AI.

 - Dirty-work appetite: you happily run the manual version today while the automation is being built. This and the automation instinct are both required; we never average them.

 - Process maturity: you've designed or owned a pipeline with throughput, SLAs, or quality bars, and you left systems running behind you - not just stories.

 - Product instinct: you can take a vague problem, figure out what's actually broken, and decide what to build or fix - without waiting for a spec or a dedicated engineering team.

 - Organized ownership: routines, follow-ups, nothing dropped. You communicate clearly, in writing and in person.

 - High agency in uncertainty: given a goal with no playbook and no owner above you, you define the problem yourself and start before permission.

 - Operating maturity: this role carries a number from week one, so it needs someone who has owned outcomes before. It is not internship-shaped.

We'll pass at any stage on candidates who only want the cool parts of the job, choose work by interestingness over impact, can't explain what an API is, or do the same manual work in month three as month one.



NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Founder or early-stage experience: you've taken something from zero, or joined early and owned a function.

 - Experience with SaaS integrations, API products, or developer-facing products.

 - Built things with agents or LLM workflows beyond personal use - tools, experiment logs, side projects other people use.

 - An engineering-adjacent path: studied engineering and moved into non-technical work, or a non-CS background with things you built on the side.

 - High-throughput ops backgrounds (delivery, marketplace, physical ops) count only alongside the AI-native bar above - on their own they are not this job.



OUTCOMES WE EXPECT IN THE FIRST 90 DAYS

description: Data Scientist/ML Job Summary Photon is hiring an experienced Data Scientist / Machine Learning Engineer, to design, build, validate, and operationalize a closed-loop Propensity-to-Pay model for Enercare Collections. The engagement runs on Enercares existing Azure platform (Azure Data Factory, ADLS, Azure Machine Learning, and Azure SQL) and reuses current ingestion and CDS integration patterns. The role owns one primary Collections model: define the pay target and scoring population, engineer features from customer, account, payment, AR, invoice, usage, delinquency, write-off, and collections history, rank accounts by likelihood to pay, and assign agreed risk segments. Scores are produced on a scheduled batch cycle, with model version and evaluation details published for CDS. Outcome and treatment feedback are brought back so cycle-over-cycle performance can show when the model should be retrained. This is a hands-on delivery role. The hire is expected to contribute from Discovery and to take the model through validation, UAT, production scoring, and handover with in agreed timeline with customer. Key Responsibilities Work with Collections business owners and data owners during Discovery to confirm the scoring population, the definition of “pay,” the prediction horizon, label history, success metrics, and acceptance thresholds. Assess whether available history, quality, and coverage can support a viable model, and document limitations, assumptions, and the baseline comparison against the current Collections prioritisation process. Define and build payment, AR, billing, customer, usage, delinquency, write-off, and collections behavioural features from the consolidated analytical dataset. Freeze the feature list with the data science lead and business owner before model build. Build and train one primary Propensity-to-Pay model, including target construction, feature selection, training, scoring, and tuning against agreed metrics. Validate technically and with the business: scoring completeness, data-leakage controls, reproducibility, output consistency, ranking and segment behaviour, calibration, and lift versus the agreed Collections baseline. Convert scores into risk segments using agreed thresholds, retain the model segment when an authorized business override is applied, and support treatment/action mapping defined by Collections. Produce a model card, validation evidence, and a reviewable scored sample for stakeholder sign-off. Implement model governance on Azure Machine Learning: unique model version identifiers, evaluation results, visibility of which version is deployed in each environment, and which version produced each scoring output. Support an alternate-version path so a candidate model can be tested in the operations layer before approval, and support controlled rollback to the previous approved version. Operationalize scheduled batch scoring with feature refresh, score generation, and controls that publish only complete, validated score sets. Failed runs must leave the last valid published scores in place. Design the closed loop: capture operational feedback and actual pay outcomes, compare performance across cycles, and recommend when retraining is required. Document what would be needed for later automated retraining; implementation beyond the agreed Collections scope is a separate change. Collaborate with data engineers on ADF, ADLS, and Azure SQL pipelines, and with QA on reconciliation of counts, score distribution, segments, and CDS output fields (customer/account key, propensity score, segment, model version, evaluation date). Use Enercare’s Azure DevOps promotion path across Development/QA, UAT, and Production. Support UAT, defect resolution, hypercare, runbook handover, and knowledge transfer. Document features, experiments, metrics, thresholds, overrides, and operating guidance so Enercare operations can run a production scoring cycle with guidance. Required Skills and Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related field. 5–8 years in data science or machine learning, including at least one classification or ranking model taken through batch scoring in production. This is a lateral hire; campus or training-only profiles will not fit the timeline. Strong Python, with day-to-day use of pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and experiment tracking. Ability to read and write SQL against large relational datasets. Solid statistics and model evaluation for imbalanced collections-style problems: target leakage, train/validation design, precision and recall at operational cut-offs, lift, calibration, stability, and segment behaviour. Hands-on Azure Machine Learning for training, model registration, versioning, and batch scoring, with data read from ADLS or Azure SQL. Experience shaping features from payment, billing, receivables, or delinquency history, and explaining ranked outputs to business stakeholders who own treatment rules. Experience writing the evidence a UAT sign-off needs: metric results, baseline comparison, scored samples, and known limitations. Clear written and spoken communication with business owners, data engineers, QA, and operations. Able to work in a fixed-scope, milestone-based delivery with Discovery, UAT, and production gates. Preferred Skills A prior propensity, credit-risk, collections, or churn model where scores drove a treatment or contact strategy. Closed-loop model monitoring: outcome labels returning after a decision, drift or performance review, and a documented retrain trigger. Azure Data Factory familiarity sufficient to trace feature-refresh and scoring pipeline dependencies, even if pipeline build sits with data engineering. MLflow or Azure ML run history, model cards, and promotion of a registered model through DevOps. Power BI or a similar tool for score-distribution and segment review with Collections stakeholders. Experience with customer/account key consolidation across more than one source before modelling. Education Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related discipline. What We Offer A defined Collections engagement with a production batch-scoring outcome, CDS consumption, and a closed-loop retraining recommendation, delivered on Azure. Direct work with data engineering, QA, DevOps, and the client Collections and CDS owners through Discovery, UAT, and hypercare. A lateral role with ownership of the model, the validation evidence, and the handover, inside a fixed 14-week program.
